Probably not. Although the Moon is geometrically well above the horizon, it is an extremely thin crescent—only **2.74% illuminated** and just **19° from the Sun**—in **bright daylight**.

At about **48° altitude**, atmospheric extinction is modest, but daylight contrast is the decisive problem. For an ordinary observer using unaided eyes and only roughly knowing where to look, this crescent would be **very difficult to detect and likely invisible**. An experienced observer with an exact position, excellent transparency, and the Sun safely blocked by a building might possibly glimpse it.

So you can reasonably expect **not to see it**, though visibility cannot be ruled out absolutely. **Do not scan near the Sun with binoculars or a telescope.**
